title: Understanding BMI: What It Really Means for Your Health

authorship.current_visible_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team
authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: What does a BMI number actually measure, and what are its limitations?
reader_intent: Understand what BMI can and cannot tell an individual about their health, and what other markers matter more.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands BMI is a population-level screening surrogate for body fatness, not an individual diagnostic, and knows its specific limitations (body composition, fat distribution, group variation).

claims.proposition: BMI cannot distinguish muscle, fat, bone, and water weight, and was designed as a population-level statistical tool, not an individual diagnostic.
claims.article_location: "What BMI Can Tell You" / "Important Limitations of BMI" sections
claims.recommended_action: Accurately matches the corpus's existing claim-bmi-surrogate-measure, though the article itself cites zero sources (no Sources section at all) — recommend citing Prentice & Jebb 2001 directly.

claims.proposition: BMI was originally developed in the 1800s by Adolphe Quetelet as a population-level statistical tool.
claims.article_location: "What BMI Is and How It Works" section
claims.recommended_action: Historically accurate (Quetelet's work on the BMI/Quetelet Index dates to the 1830s-1840s) but stated without a citation.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Directly supports the 'look beyond BMI' message with concrete alternative markers.
Complementary broader framing of health beyond a single number.

disposition_reason: Accurate and well-aligned with the corpus's own verified claim-bmi-surrogate-measure, but has zero citations of any kind despite being a claims-bearing definitional article — the easiest possible fix is adding the Prentice & Jebb 2001 citation the corpus already has verified.
required_research: None — the supporting source (src-prentice-jebb-2001) already exists in the registry; this is a citation-attachment task, not new research.
recommended_rewrite_scope: Add a Sources section citing Prentice & Jebb 2001 directly for the BMI-as-surrogate claim.
